sections.title: GM #1 — Crew Expectations — January 1, 2026 [corridor]
sections.text:
US EAST DIVISION  ISSUED: January 1, 2026 
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 1   
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1 
NOTICES CANCELLED:    
TO:  ALL T&E Employees 
          RE:    Crew Expectations  
 
Road Switchers 
• Crews will report dressed and ready to commence work at start of shift 
• Engineer and brakeman will proceed directly to the locomotive(s), on board within 10 
minutes of on duty time 
o Engineer will make a full service automatic brake reduction and release to signal that 
they are on the locomotive 
o Perform inspection and air brake test (as required) 
• Conductor will contact supervisor to conduct job briefing regarding work to be completed 
within 2 minutes of on duty time 
• Crew will perform job briefing on locomotive 
• Wheels turning within 20 minutes of on duty time 
o Any impediment to these standards will be documented on the delay report and 
escalated to appropriate supervisor. 
• Meal Durations 
o 20 minute meal period 
o Movement will be commenced at expiration of meal period (30 minutes wheel stop to 
wheel start). Any issues preventing this movement will be documented on delay report 
and escalated to supervisor 
• Delay report will be kept with detailed description of any delay exceeding 5 minutes 
 
 Yard Assignments 
• Crews will report dressed and ready to commence work at start of shift 
• Engineer and helper/switchman will proceed directly to the locomotive(s), on board within 
5 minutes  
o Engineer will make a full service automatic brake reduction and release to signal they 
are on the locomotive 
o Perform inspection and air brake test (as required) 
• Conductor will contact General Yardmaster for instructions within 2 minutes of shift start for 
instructions 
• Wheels turning within 10 minutes of on duty time 
• 20 minute meal period 
o 30 minutes allowed from wheel stop to wheel start  
o Any issues that prevent movement will be escalated to Yardmaster or Manager
Road Crews 
• Crews will report dressed and ready to commence work at start of shift 
• Paperwork will be pulled or obtained (i.e. Ready packets) within 2 minutes of on duty time 
• If documents are unavailable immediately escalate to appropriate supervisor and 
document on delay report 
• Engineers of originating trains will proceed directly to the locomotive(s), on board within 10 
minutes of on duty time 
o Engineer will make a full service automatic brake reduction and release to signal that 
they are on the locomotive 
o Perform inspection and air brake test (as required) 
• Run through trains performing change off will perform a job briefing and be ready to 
proceed within 5 minutes 
• Any delay exceeding 5 minutes or situation preventing adherence to standards will be 
documented on delay report 
 
 
Working with Student Conductors 
While working in the field with a Student Conductor as part of your crew, it is very important for 
the Conductor to teach the Student the proper way to perform different tasks of the job and 
how to remain safe while performing these tasks in the field. The Student Conductor should 
always be within close proximity of the Conductor on the job and not used as a Brakeman or 
helper. Regardless of their skill level, how far along they are in their training, or previous 
employment, this is for their safety and they should also be able to demonstrate that they are 
able to perform the tasks of the job to the Conductor that is training them. 
 
 
 
No Vacancy at Primary Hotels 
When contacting Crew Management, you must call in using the VRU 1-888-225-5127.  If unable 
to complete your task through the self-serve menu, you can select to be transferred to the crew 
dispatcher and your call will be answered in the order it is received. 
 
In the event that the primary hotel is out of rooms, crews must contact facilities at 1-877-805-8588 
to arrange alternate lodging. 
o Do not release cab until you’ve confirmed that primary hotel has rooms available, 
to avoid additional delay if needing to go to alternate hotel. 
  
If unable to get through after 10 minutes please contact CMC so that it can be escalated to the 
current manager on duty. 
 
Notifying CMC of Late Transportation  
Arrange to notify crew management if you are waiting on transportation for more than 10 
minutes past your on duty time or the required need time of your transportation.  
 
If you are on a train or need to use the radio to make the notification that you have been 
waiting for your transportation, contact the train dispatcher who will relay the information to 
crew management.
Company Physical Requirements 
Employees booking off for a company physical need to schedule the appointment on a 
Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday.  CMC will need to be notified once the appointment is made. 
 
If your total time of covered service is greater than twelve (12) hours, it is your responsibility and 
expectation that you report the Hours of Service Violation to your local manager and Manager 
of Crew Management.  You may contact Sterling Joppru, CMC Manager at 612-904-5803 to 
report all HOS Violations. 
 
It is also the employee’s responsibility to report time spent at a company physical.  This can be 
done by creating an Hours of Service Record in FRA Certification.  This can be done by creating 
an “OT” event.  It’s also the employee’s responsibility to be properly rested prior to and after the 
event.  If you have questions about any FRA issues, please call CMC and they will assist you.   
 
Availability Standards & 7-Day Mark Bid Preference System  
When laying off sick, T&E and Yardmaster employees must call the VRU (888-225-5127) to reach 
CMC. 
 
For Canadian Pacific to be successful and competitive in the North American Railway industry 
we not only have to provide great customer service, we have to continue our collective efforts 
at exceling on efficiency and productivity.  Given that efficiency and productivity are directly 
impacted by employee attendance levels, an attendance policy that is understood and 
adhered to by all is essential.   
  
Effective February 1, 2017 for T&E employees and January 1, 2019 for Yardmaster employees, the 
following availability standard supersedes and replaces all previous availability standards for T&E 
and Yardmaster employees at Canadian Pacific.   
 
T&E and Yardmaster employees have negotiated opportunities provided for in their Collective 
Agreements to legitimately remove themselves from the working board. Examples of negotiated 
and also legal absence categories that will not result in discipline under this availability standard 
include: annual vacation; pre-authorized personal leave; bereavement; jury duty; company 
business; and time off mandated by the hours of service regulations as amended by the Rail 
Safety Improvement Act. 
 
T&E and Yardmaster employees who book off sick or unpaid personal leave on two or more 
available work days in the calendar month will be subject to attendance review for that month. 
Disciplinary action may result. 
 
The following absence categories will be handled as more serious offenses separate from this 
calendar month review:  
 
• Miss calls (including missing calls as an ESB / demoted Engineer);  
• Booking sick or unfit on-call or after accepting a call;  
• Booking sick or unfit after call time or after start time of assignment;  
• Refusals to protect service;  
• Not reporting or reporting late for duty;  
• Unauthorized absence (AWOL);
• Exhibiting a pattern of booking sick on weekends or consecutive to other absence types, 
such as, but not limited to: vacation, paid leave, and rest days.  
• More than 12 sick absences within one calendar year 
 
Note: Medical documentation will not be accepted to excuse these absence categories 
except in extraordinary circumstances involving a documented medical emergency. 
 
Employees requesting to have sick absences excused due to their own serious medical issues 
must ensure that satisfactory medical information is received by Health Services for review within 
three (3) business days from the last day of the medical absence. The three-business day 
requirement will be strictly enforced. Upon receipt of timely and satisfactory information, the 
request will be reviewed to determine if the absence has been substantiated. Employees 
seeking leaves under FMLA or accommodations under the ADA should comply with the 
procedures in those policies.  
 
Health Services fax number is 1-800-933-8833. 
Health Services email address is CP_HealthServicesDocuments@cpkcr.com 
 
7-Day Mark Bid Preference – PIN Requirement  
 
 Effective July 22, 2023 you will be required to create a Personal Identification Number (PIN) 
to access the 7-Day Mark Bid Preference System. The system will be unavailable at 1900 hours 
CST July 21 for approx. 2 hours while this change is implemented.  
 
NOTE: it is important that all employees access the system as soon as possible after the effective 
date to create your PIN and thereby protect access to your personal bid information.  
 
 
Follow the below steps to create your PIN:  
• At the Sign-in screen, enter your employee number and exit the field.
• System will prompt you to enter a PIN between 6 and 10 numbers in length consistent 
with the listed rules. 
 
 
 
 
• Click Submit  
• Upon successful PIN creation, you will be directed back to the Sign-in screen. Enter 
employee number, PIN and check the User Agreement Box to access the system. 
 
 
Follow the below steps if you need to reset your PIN:  
• Click Request PIN Reset (shown in Red on Sign-in screen).
You will then see the following menu: 
 
 
• Click Send Email.You will receive an email titled “Crew 7 Day Mark – PIN Reset Request” 
at the email address listed in the 7-Day Mark Bid Preference System. 
 
 
• Click the Reset button in this email and the PIN will reset to your employee number. You 
will then be prompted to create a new PIN at your next Login.
Note: If you do not have a correct email listed in the system, click the Contact Timekeeper 
button to send an email to the Timekeeping department.  They will reset the PIN to your 
employee number.   
Email addresses can be updated directly in the job selection screen. 
 
 
Crew Office – Methods of Contact 
• Employees being called utilizing the VRU 
o the number will show as the following 403-260-5800 (please add to contacts to avoid 
being marked as spam) 
• Employees being called directly by Crew Dispatcher 
o The number will show as the following 612-607-0150 or 612-338-5004 (please add to 
contacts to avoid being marked as spam) 
• The old direct lines that were used by many are no longer in service, all calls to the crew 
office will need to be done by calling the VRU which requires a PIN to do so (instructions 
below) 
• To declare drop turn without calling into the crew office please send email to following 
CMC0143@CPKCR.COM 
o This is for drop turns only 
• Calling in to the Shift Supervisor line for Crew Dispatcher needs will be transferred back to 
the CD line, please ensure using this number for emergencies only. 
For those employees who have not yet established permanent PIN numbers, please listen 
carefully to the prompts on the VRU. You will be asked to enter your employee number followed 
by the temporary PIN number assigned to you. Once you have entered that number, you will be 
required to establish your own personal PIN. The PIN you establish will be the one you will use for 
future calls to the VRU. 
 
In addition, please be advised of the following security considerations regarding the validation 
of PIN numbers: 
• Employee must enter a minimum PIN length – must be 4 to 7 digits. 
• Your PIN cannot be the last 4 digits of your employee number. 
• If the PIN number is 4 digits, it must contain at least four different numbers. (ie. 1212 is not a valid 
PIN number) 
• If the PIN number is 5 digits or more, it must not contain more than two consecutive repeated 
digits. (The number must contain 4 different digits) 
• The same PIN must not to be used in the last four PIN changes. 
 
 
Booking Off Investigation Requirement 
Effective immediately, employees being called by CMC for an assignment that are already 
scheduled for a formal investigation are to book off in status “I” and hold themselves out if the 
assignment the employee is being called for would impact their ability to be rested and attend 
the formal investigation.
Reporting Delays  
Timely notification of delays is imperative to improved operations, updated line ups and increased train 
speed.  While operating across the BNSF Twin Cities Terminal (Humboldt to St Croix) please escalate 
delays between Shoreham and St Paul via radio to the MN Dispatcher and delays between St Paul and St 
Croix via radio to the River Train Dispatcher.   
 
If you have questions please ask the Superintendent. 
 
 
Wearing Hooded Clothing  
Employees who choose to wear clothing with hoods (i.e. hoodies, winter parkas, jackets, etc.) must 
ensure the hood when worn does not interfere with your vision (as per Functional Safety Rules Personal 
Protective Equipment and Clothing).  
Correct Way to Wear Hoods 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Top of the hood be placed on the crown of the head with the fabric pulled back behind the eyes so 
that peripheral vision is not restricted.  
 
To assist with placement of hood: 
o Use the draw string on the garment to secure the hood in a position to prevent vision from 
being restricted.  
o Wearing the hood over the top of a ball cap or hard hat will assist in keeping the hood back to 
avoid obstructing peripheral vision. 
 
Incorrect Way to Wear Hoods 
           
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Hood fabric should not be pulled so far forward in front of the eyes so that peripheral vision is 
restricted.
Fuel Readings from Yard Locomotives  
Fuel readings from all locomotives on road trains are required to be reported to the Train Dispatcher: 
 
-Outbound crews must report levels upon departure from a crew change location. 
-Inbound crews on arrival at the train’s final destination. 
-Whenever a train is being fueled inbound and outbound fuel levels must be reported. 
 
The only exception to this requirement is if getting fuel levels on Distributed Power will delay the train- If 
this is the case levels on Distributed power are not required but headend levels must still be reported to 
the Train Dispatcher. 
 
Local, RCO and Yard assignments are exempt. 
 
 
Weather Below Freezing Temperatures 
Effective immediately, anytime temperatures require locomotives to be left running, all heaters inside the  
RCL Locomotives and DP remote power should be left on and remain on until the unit is no longer 
required to be left running.  
 
 
Conditioning Brakes at Crew Change Locations  
Inbound locomotive engineers must condition the train brakes using the automatic brake at the following 
crew change locations: 
1. Ottumwa 
2. Savanna 
3. St. Paul 
4. Minnesota City 
  
The results of train brake conditioning must be documented on the crew information form and 
communicated to the outbound locomotive engineer, when present. 
 
Zip Tie Auto Racks  
Effective immediately, all auto racks will be zip tied to ensure reliability over the road.  This will ensure: 
1. A Safer more reliable fleet. 
2. A reduction of service interruptions related to warm wheels, air leaks, air hose failure, and set offs. 
3. An increase in train speed.  
4. A reduction of cost associated with delays and 
5. Ensure the safety of our employee by preventing the need to walk trains. 
6. This directive includes all Autos that are attached to engines.
Dial-Up Tones for Outline Point Yardmasters 
Effective February 12, 2025, dial up tone “7” will call the Outline Point Yardmaster for the following yards 
and channels at those yards:  
 
 
Glenwood 44 88 84 94 65 341/465 
Humboldt/Shoreham 65 94 84 341/465 
Muskego/Milwaukee 65 88 41 84 44 320/484 
Duluth 44 
Superior 44 94 
 
 
Emergency Notification Process  
This notice serves as a reminder to all T&E employees of the Emergency Notification procedure. In the 
event of a family emergency while you are working, family members should contact the CPKC Public 
Safety Communications Center at 1-800-716-9132 and select option 1. This call center is staffed 24/7 and 
will be able to appropriately dispatch the call to ensure prompt notification of family emergencies as 
necessary. 
 
Please be mindful that this line is for emergencies only and should not be used for general 
communication that can wait until you are off duty. 
 
 
 
Calls to Work from Crew Management  
When crew management calls T&E to work there will now only be two numbers contacting you 
 
• Calls sent using automated dialer will show as 403-260-5800 
• Manual attempts will show as 888-225-5127(same # used to check standing) 
 
Ensure you have Crew Management saved as a contact with both #s in that contact 
 
See below how to set contact to bypass do not disturb/silent preventing missed calls
iPhone users  
If there’s an individual contact who you want to hear from, but they are not on your Favorites list, you can 
still make an exception to Do Not Disturb on a person-by-person basis. 
 
• Open Contacts 
• Select the entry for the person you want to bypass DND 
• Tap “Edit” in the card’s upper right corner 
• Scroll down to “Ringtone” and tap it 
• At the top of the next card, toggle Emergency Bypass to “on.” That allows calls from that person to 
bypass Do Not Disturb. 
• Tap Done 
 
 
Android users 
• Press and hold do not disturb icon 
• Click details 
• Enable do not disturb 
• Under allowed during do not disturb click calls and messages 
• Click add contact and select whatever you have CMC contact saved as 
Click Done after selecting contact 
 
 
Crossing Tracks While Operating Kubota  
All T&E employees operating Kubota-style vehicles will need to make a complete stop and check both 
directions to ascertain that there is no conflicting movement before proceeding over and railroad 
crossings.  
 
This includes all crossings in the yard, whether it be vehicle crossing, mechanical crossings, or any other 
type of makeshift rail crossing that has been installed.  
 
 
Mounting & Dismounting Stationary Equipment – Buddy System  
When mounting and dismounting Locomotives that are stationary the following practice is to be adhered to: 
 
Utilization of the buddy system when more than one employee is mounting or dismounting: 
Compliance with T19 in addition to the Buddy System: 
 
1. Prior to mounting dismounting employees are to Job Brief about how to safely perform loading or unloading 
of items.  Size, weight, weather and body positioning to prevent exertion are to be discussed.  Items that 
prevent you from maintaining 3 points of contact or obstruct how you hold the hand hold properly will be 
handed up and down. For example, backpacks that are properly worn can be left on, cases of water, 
markers, or oversized tools, must be handed up and down using the buddy system.   
 
2. Any items that cannot be safely handled, or properly stored because of shape or weight are prohibited.
Instructions for Rollby Inspections  
When crews are required to do a rollby after a crew change is performed, and the train has not started moving 
within 15 minutes, the inbound crew is relieved of rollby duties and is now governed by local instruction.  
 
If you have any questions, please contact local managers. 
 
T&E Joint Industry Customers – Reporting inventory Changes  
Effective immediately, a new enhancement has been released in the CPKC Customer Station portal, 
impacting our joint industry (JIND) customers and how railcars are reported in AIR 2.0 & TYES. 
 
What’s Changing? 
Class Coding: For joint industry customers, railcars previously class coded with a JIND or JI suffix in 
AIR/TYES will now be reported as Placed (PACT).  
 
Visibility: These cars will remain visible in AIR 2.0, TYES and Customer Station unless they are reported 
as traveling on a foreign railroad. At this point, they will be removed/deleted from inventory. 
 
Note: There are no changes for non-joint industry customers. 
 
Why is this important? 
• Railcars placed at joint industries will remain visible in CPKC systems. 
• Customer can now use the Customer Station portal to request supplemental activities such as 
intra-plant switching at these locations. 
• In addition to planned supplemental work, unplanned work like “Switch to Another/Same Track” or 
“Move for Switch” can now be directly reported using the AIR iPad. 
 
Should you have any questions, speak with your manager. 
 
 
7-Day Mark – Bidding to Extra Boards – BLET Only  
Pursuant to the updated SOO BLET Agreement, effective for the mark of December 27, 2025, Engineers may 
move within an Extra Board if that board is on a 5/2 or 4/3 schedule.  
 
This means you must bid specific Extra Board turn numbers (1,2,3, etc.,), same as for a Sadie Hawkins mark.   
 
If you fail to bid turn numbers, you will NOT be awarded a position on a 5/2 or 4/3 Extra Board unless by 
default.   
 
The “XTRA” designation only applies to a 6/2 Extra Board during a regular (non-Sadie Hawkins) mark period. 
 
Best practice is to include both turn numbers and the “XTRA” designation in your bid menu.
We will all go Home Safe; Working Safely Together.  
 
 
Work smart, stay safe. 
  
Jacob Rinnels  
General Manager 
U.S. East Operations

sections.title: GM #2 — Clear Cab Procedures — January 1, 2026
sections.text:
US EAST DIVISION  ISSUED: January 1, 2026 
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 2 
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-2 
NOTICES CANCELLED:    
TO:  ALL T&E Employees 
          RE:    Clear Cab Procedures 
 
To maintain our commitment to operate safely, changes are being made to the way we communicate in 
certain situations under the “Clear Cab” initiative. The clear cab initiative is a means to facilitate proper 
job briefings prior to engaging in an operationally sensitive activity (listed below).  The briefing will be held 
and then documented on the updated Road Briefing Form. 
 
 
1. Restricted Speed/Other than main track  
When operating in an area or beyond a signal requiring movement to be able to stop within half the 
range of vision is governed by the following: 
  
▪ Prior to entry of the restricted area all crew members in the controlling cab must remain in a 
position to observe all forward movement (e.g. not in nose of locomotive).  
▪ Job briefing must be held covering the following:  
‒ Requirements of applicable rule GCOR 6.27 Restricted Speed or GCOR 6.28 Other than Main 
Track;  
‒ Territorial issues such as switches, areas of reduced visibility, curves, and grade;  
‒ Speed;  
and 
‒ Duties of crew members.  
 
▪ Update the “Clear Cab - Operational Sensitive Activities” portion on the back page of the Road 
Briefing Form. 
▪ After briefing has been completed radio transmission must be made as follows:  
‒ Train or engine identification, location, “proceeding per rule ____ (6.27 or 6.28)____, at a speed 
that allows movement to stop within half the range of vision.”  
− When entering a yard into 6.28 Other Than Main Track territory, you only have to make the 
announcement at the entry point. Radio transmission is no longer required once the 
Locomotive is no longer on the Main Track. 
▪ While operating at restricted/other than main track speed crew members must not perform tasks 
unrelated to operation until stopped, or no longer under restriction.”
2. Form B/Track Out of Service   
5 miles prior to entry into the limits of a Form B or Track Out of Service, be governed by the following: 
  
▪ All crew members in the controlling cab of the locomotive must remain in a position to observe all 
forward movements (e.g. not in nose of locomotive).  
▪ Job briefing must be held covering the following:  
‒ Location of yellow/red and red flag; 
‒ Limits of restriction;  
‒ Start and end time of restriction;  
‒ Employee in charge;  
‒ Where stop will be made if communication with employee in charge is unsuccessful; 
and  
‒ Duties of crew members.  
▪ Once briefing is complete update the “Clear Cab - Operational Sensitive Activities” portion on the 
back page of the Road Briefing Form.  
▪ As movement approaches the restricted area crew members must not perform any tasks 
unrelated to operation until stopped, or no longer restricted.  
 
 
3. Temporary Speed Restriction / Radio Bulletin  
5 miles prior to entry of an area restricted by radio bulletin or speed restriction be governed as follows:  
▪ All crew members in the controlling cab of the locomotive must remain in a position to observe all 
forward movements (e.g. not in nose of locomotive).  
▪ Job briefing must be held covering the following:  
‒ MP location of restriction;  
‒ Type of restriction (e.g. Crossing malfunction, temporary speed restriction, etc.);  
‒ Operation concerns;  
‒ Speed on the approach to and through restricted area;  
and 
‒ Duties of crew members. 
  
▪ Once briefing is complete update the “Clear Cab - Operational Sensitive Activities” portion on the 
back page of the Road Briefing Form  
▪ As movement approaches the restricted area crew members must not perform any tasks 
unrelated to operation until stopped, or no longer restricted  
 
4. Approaching STOP indication (CTC) or end of Track Warrant Authority (TWC)  
After passing a signal indication (CTC) that will require the movement to proceed prepared to stop such 
as  
GCOR 9.1.4 Approach or 9.1.9 Diverging Approach, will be governed by the following:
▪ All crew members in the controlling cab of the locomotive must remain in a position to observe all 
forward movements (e.g. not in nose of locomotive).  
▪ Job briefing must be held regarding the following:  
‒ Signal aspect; 
and  
‒ Location stop may be required.  
▪ Radio transmission must be made as follows:  
‒ Train or engine identification, (Signal aspect) at (Location), proceeding prepared to stop at 
(Location).  
▪ As movement approaches the area where the train may be required to stop crew members must 
not perform any tasks unrelated to the operation until stopped, or no longer restricted.  
▪ Once stop is made the following must be transmitted over the radio:  
‒ Train or engine identification, stopped at Location, for (signal indication).  
 
5 miles prior to the end of track warrant authority (TWC) be governed by the following:  
▪ All crew members in the controlling cab of the locomotive must remain in a position to observe all 
forward movements (e.g. not in nose of locomotive).  
▪ Job briefing must be conducted covering the following:  
‒ Current authority and end of limits;  
‒ Where stop will be made if additional authority is not received;  
‒ Speed;  
and 
‒ Duties of crew members.  
 
▪ Once briefing is complete update the “Clear Cab - Operational Sensitive Activities” portion on the 
back page of the Road Briefing Form.  
 
▪ Radio transmission must be made as follows: 
‒ Train or engine identification, approaching the end of track warrant authority (number) 
proceeding prepared to stop at (location) 
 
▪ As movement approaches the restricted area, crew members must not perform any tasks 
unrelated to operation until stopped, or no longer restricted.  
Exception: 
 
▪ Mandatory directives may be copied or released in during aforementioned operationally sensitive 
activities after completion of the following: 
‒ Job briefing has been conducted;  
and 
‒ all crew members in the controlling cab agree that such action will not adversely affect safe 
operation of the train.

We will all go Home Safe; Working Safely Together.  
 
 
Work smart, stay safe. 
  
Jacob Rinnels  
General Manager 
U.S. East Operations

sections.title: GM #3 — Fuel Conservation — January 1, 2026
sections.text:
US EAST DIVISION  ISSUED: January 1, 2026 
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 3 
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-3 
NOTICES CANCELLED:    
TO:  ALL T&E Employees 
          RE:    Fuel Conservation   
 
Until further notice, Conductors are required to document Fuel Trip Optimizer (FTO) usage on the Train 
Delay Report. This information will be gathered by conducting required job briefings with the Locomotive 
Engineer and other assigned crew members.  
 
FTO Documentation Requirements 
• Initialization status indicating failure or success 
• Time and location(s) operating in manual control 
• Enter remarks in chronological order (where possible) 
o Example: FTO is returned to manual control enroute while slowing for a train meet 
▪ Indicate time and milepost range where auto control was not used 
• Confirm defects or system issues have been reported as required  
 
 
This information will assist by improving visibility to situations where auto control cannot be maintained, 
allow corrective actions to be leveraged to increase system utilization, and control costs through the 
reduction of fuel expenditures. 
 
If you have any questions, contact your local Road Foreman for assistance.  
 
 
 
Throttle Restrictions 
To continue CPKC’s efforts in fuel conservation, throttle restrictions are being introduced to subdivisions 
across Canada and US for all non-FTO trains. This will ensure that consists run based on planned HPT and 
avoid excess fuel costs. Local bulletins will outline directional restrictions for each subdivision.  
 
The restrictions will apply based on a train’s Horsepower Per Ton (HPT) ratio. 
The Train Tonnage Report provides information on locomotive horsepower:
To calculate HPT: 
1. Add the horsepower of all online locomotives. 
2. Divide by the Equivalent Gross Tonnage (E.G.T.). 
 
Example: 
8800 HP / 16706 tons = 0.53 HPT 
If you require assistance with calculating HPT, please contact the Dispatcher. 
 
Throttle Restrictions 
  The following restriction applies to trains 241 and 577 that are not operating in FTO: 
            If HPT of train consist is greater than 1.7, throttle notch restriction is 6. 
This restriction only applies at speeds over 20 mph.  If a higher throttle is required to prevent train 
stalling, advise the Dispatcher. 
 
 
 
Trains 180/181 
All 180/181 train symbols are to isolate locomotives as follows:  
 
• Only one locomotive can be online per 3640 tons.  
• Trains over 3640 tons may have two locomotives online.  
 
Additional locomotives in the head end consist are to be isolated first. If additional locomotives are 
present, idle the tail end remote first, then mid-train remote(s) as applicable.  
 
To prevent a stall on a Heavy or Mountain grade, one additional locomotive may be placed online. 
When placing a locomotive back online, select a remote locomotive first (where applicable). Such 
locomotive must be isolated immediately once the movement has ascended the grade.  
 
In FTO operation:  
• Trains required to ISOLATE trailing units must continue to run using FTO.  
• Trains required to IDLE remotes shall also run FTO by taking advantage of a new  
 
FTO feature that allows the last remote to be idled while in FTO. This new button is in the FTO “Restrictions” 
page.  
 
 
 
If this button is not available, trains required to IDLE their remote must run manual.

Work smart, stay safe.

General Manager 
U.S. East Operations

US EAST DIVISION                                                             ISSUED: January 1, 2026

NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-6

TO: ALL T&E Employees 
RE: Away From Home Terminal & Hours of Service   
 
When crews arrive at their Away From Home Terminal (AFHT) they are to tie up at that 
location as this is the location that they are off duty. Once you are tied up per Federal 
Regulation, the railroad has 30 minutes from the time you go off duty to get you to the 
lodging facility which is considered Time Off Duty. When you are called for duty at the 
AFHT, the time that you are called for is the time that you are to be at the on duty 
location, not the time that you depart from the lodging facility. 
 
The following information is from the Federal Railroad Administration Hours of Service 
Compliance Manual. 
 
Away From Home Terminal   
• FRA allows 30 minutes for commuting at the AFHT for travel between the release or 
on-duty location and lodging facility.  (OP-04-29)  
 
Travel to the on-duty location from lodging at the AFHT  
• One-way travel time greater than 30 minutes, including delays associated with 
transportation, will be considered as a deadhead to duty and counts as time on duty.    
 
Note:  The time a crew is delayed for personal reasons, such as stopping to buy items 
at a store or stopping to eat at a restaurant, will not count toward the 30-minute 
allowance.  
 
Travel from the release location to lodging at the AFHT  
• One-way travel time greater than 30 minutes, including delays associated with 
transportation and lodging availability, will be considered as a deadhead from duty to a 
point of final release and counts as neither time on duty nor time off duty (limbo time).
Note:  The time a crew is delayed for personal reasons, such as stopping to buy items 
at a store, or stopping to eat at a restaurant, will not count toward the 30-minute 
allowance.  When an employee exceeds the 30-minute allowance traveling to lodging, 
he or she must contact the railroad and give an updated release time.

US EAST DIVISION                                                          ISSUED: January 19, 2026 
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 14 
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-14 
NOTICES CANCELLED:  
TO: ALL T&E EMPLOYEES 
RE: Vehicle Operations 
 
Pre-Trip Vehicle Requirements 
Before operating a vehicle for company business, drivers must: 
1. Conduct a 360-degree walk-around inspection to identify hazards, obstructions, or 
unsafe conditions. 
2. Complete all required daily vehicle inspection reports prior to use. 
3. Immediately report unsafe conditions, defects, or damage to a supervisor. 
4. Remove defective vehicles from service until repaired or properly tagged. 
 
2. General Operating Requirements 
1. Drivers are fully accountable for the safe and controlled operation of the vehicle. 
2. Passengers are required to verbally alert the driver if unsafe conditions or behaviors are 
observed. 
3. Seat belts must be worn by all occupants at all times when equipped. 
4. Headlights or daytime running lights must be on while the vehicle is in operation. 
5. Vehicles must not be operated with doors open or while entering/exiting a moving 
vehicle. 
6. All tools, materials, and equipment must be properly secured. This includes laptops.  
 
3. Mobile Device Use 
1. Company-issued cell phones may be used hands-free only and solely for company 
business when: 
o It is safe to do so, and 
o Such use is permitted by applicable state, provincial, or local laws. 
2. Personal cell phones are prohibited while operating company vehicles unless: 
o Explicit authorization is granted, and 
o A company phone has not been provided. 
 
 
 
 
 
4. Parking & Reversing Safety 
1. Pull-through parking must be used when available. 
2. When pull-through parking is unavailable, vehicles should be backed into parking spaces
unless unsafe. 
3. Vehicles may not be parked within six (6) feet of railroad tracks unless proper protection 
is in place. 
4. Unattended vehicles must be: 
o Secured against movement (park, brake set, chocks if required) 
o Turned off with keys removed 
o Locked with all compartments and windows closed 
 
 
Failure to comply with this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including loss of 
driving privileges, corrective action, or termination.

Work smart, stay safe.

sections.title: GM #18 — 2026 Weed & Brush Spray Program — March 31, 2026
sections.text:
US EAST DIVISION                                                          ISSUED: March 31, 2026   
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 18    
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-18 
NOTICES CANCELLED:  
TO: ALL T&E EMPLOYEES 
RE: 2026 Weed & Brush Spray Program   
 
Starting the week of April 6th and continuing for the next six months RWC will be spraying 
herbicides in CP’s Southern Region to control vegetation. This vegetation control is to improve 
working conditions, to remove health and safety hazards, to maintain proper drainage, to permit 
proper inspection of track, to provide safe walkways, maintain a professional appearance and to 
reduce fire hazards. 
 
Depending on the location in Southern Region, a mixture of two or more of the following 
herbicides may be used: Esplanade, Oust Extra, Method 240SL, Vista XRT, Roundup Pro 
Concentrate, TerraVue, Piper EZ, Plateau, Polaris AC. 
 
Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS), for these herbicides can be obtained from Field Ops 
Manager’s Office, Engineering Services Supervisors Office, local Field Safety Coordinator or 
https://intranet.cpr.ca/worktools/Pages/Applications/Material-Safety-Data-Sheets-MSDS.aspx. Location 
where each of the above herbicides will be used can be obtained from the Vegetation 
Management Specialist by calling 318-440-8917. Industrial Hygiene has reviewed these MSDS 
and advises that the herbicides have a low health risk when applied by a licensed contractor. 
While the herbicides used have a low health risk, the following safety precautions should be 
taken during the herbicide application: 
 
❖ Stay out of the area being sprayed. 
❖ Stand upwind during application to avoid breathing sprays and mists. 
❖ Do not re-enter spray area for 30 minutes. 
❖ As an extra pre-caution it is recommended that for one full week, or until a heavy rain 
has washed the residual material off switch stands, track, etc, wear impervious gloves 
when working in the spray area and wash hands before eating or smoking and prior to 
leaving work.  
 
To reduce any skin contact with freshly sprayed vegetation, it is recommended that for the first 
24 hours after spraying, any employee required to walk or work in these recently sprayed areas 
wear impervious gloves, shoes plus socks, long sleeved shirts with the sleeves rolled down, and 
to launder this day’s clothing before re-wearing them. 
 
Your understanding and consideration will assist your fellow employees in providing and 
receiving timely information essential to their work assignments.
We will all go Home Safe; Working Safely Together. 
 
 
Work smart, stay safe. 
Jacob Rinnels  
General Manager

US EAST DIVISION                                                          ISSUED: April 15, 2026   
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 20   
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-20 
NOTICES CANCELLED:  
TO: ALL T&E EMPLOYEES 
RE:   EEBA Inspection & Training  
 
MANDATORY EEBA INSPECTION BEFORE EVERY TOUR OF DUTY 
All US crew members must inspect their assigned Emergency Escape Breathing Apparatus (EEBA) using 
the iPad EEBA Inspection App or FIT Kiosk before starting any tour of duty.  
Unless otherwise instructed, EEBA use is required when performing train service of any type. This 
includes yard assignments, deadhead service, and taxi travel.  
In Canada and Mexico, crews are only required to inspect and carry an EEBA when originating-from or 
destined-to a Canada–US or Mexico–US border location, including when deadheading. Follow local 
instructions for EEBA use. 
 
HOW TO INSPECT YOUR EEBA 
• Open the EEBA App on your iPad or use a FIT Kiosk. 
• Log in using your CPKC User ID (do not use a KCS User ID). 
o Inspections must be completed using your own login and the device you are personally 
using. 
• Scan your assigned EEBA or enter the serial number. 
o Do not scan or record inspections on behalf of another employee. 
• Perform the inspection. 
o Each crew member must inspect and scan their own assigned EEBA. 
• Record the result (Pass/Fail) in the app. 
 
In Canada and Mexico, crews must inspect the EEBA issued to them, including units signed out from 
lockers. 
  
IF THE APP OR DEVICE IS UNAVAILABLE 
Use the EEBA Manual Inspection Form (paper log) available at your terminal. 
• Fill out all required fields. 
• Submit the completed form before departure. 
• Notify your local manager. 
  
FAILED INSPECTION? 
Do NOT proceed with a failed EEBA. 
Immediately notify your local manager and get a replacement and/or follow further instructions.
TRAINING & SUPPORT 
The following EEBA training is mandatory: 
• Course 3940.4 – EEBA for US Train Crews – Online 
• Course 3940.5 – EEBA for US Train Crews – French Online 
• Course 3440.6 – EEBA for US Train Crews – Spanish Online 
 
Job aids and inspection manuals are available on CPKC SharePoint under “Operations Training 
Materials” 
 
For assistance, contact your supervisor. For technical assistance, contact the Help Desk. 
 
 
We will all go Home Safe; Working Safely Together. 
 
 
Work smart, stay safe.
